chunks: And that which was narrated is: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya from Abu Ja'far from his father from Ghiyath ibn Ibrahim from Ja'far from his father, who said:
I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him): Should I begin with Medina or with Mecca? He said, 'Begin with Mecca and conclude with Medina, for that is superior.'

This is applicable to one who performs Hajj via a route other than this, either from Syria or Yemen or others; but as for one who performs Hajj via the route of Iraq, the superior method is what we have mentioned.
And it has been narrated that he may do whichever he wishes, and this does not contradict that beginning with Medina is superior; rather, it indicates the removal of prohibition in that matter.

key_terms.طَرِيقِ اَلْعِرَاقِ: The route of Iraq (a specific geographical path for Hajj)

ai.seo_question: What is the recommended order for visiting Mecca and Medina during Hajj according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the jurisprudential nuance between the optimal (afdhal) and obligatory (wajib) aspects of the Hajj itinerary, distinguishing between the general permissibility of any route and the specific merit of starting with Mecca for those not coming from Iraq. The text highlights the scholarly tradition of reconciling apparent contradictions by distinguishing between absolute preference and the removal of prohibition (raf' al-hazr), ensuring that flexibility in travel routes does not negate the spiritual superiority of the recommended sequence.
